summary: Adds the Garmin loopback SSO sign-in, the DI OAuth2 exchange and pre-call refresh, an identity assertion that refuses a token from the wrong account, and a one-time migration of the pre-press token file. Wired from internal/cli/root.go: registerNovelCommand runs configureGarminAuth, which replaces the generated auth setup/status/logout and hides set-token; registerClientHook runs installGarminFreshToken, which refreshes an about-to-expire token before the first API call for CLI commands and for internal/mcp/tools.go, which calls cli.ApplyClientHooks on the client it builds directly; addNovelCommandIfAbsent registers auth login, the generator's own novel-command scaffold with its RunE implemented in place as its header invites. No generated code was edited. REPRINT NOTE: the SKILL.md '## Auth Setup' block and the README '## Authentication' section are generated bearer-token boilerplate that a reprint restores; listing them in files[] does NOT preserve them (verified by control regen). Re-apply the auth-login choreography to SKILL.md and README.md by hand after every reprint until the upstream SKILL.md template honours the scheme's x-auth-instructions.
reason: Garmin issues no personal API token, so the generated bearer-token contract (auth setup / auth set-token prose about pasting a key) describes a credential that does not exist. The spec declares a plain bearer scheme with no token_url, so the generator emitted no refreshAccessToken at all: without a hand-authored refresh the stored token dies after roughly 22 hours. The identity assertion exists because a browser that is already signed in to another household member's Garmin account silently returns that account's ticket, and nothing in the token itself names the account.
validated_outcome: go build ./..., go vet ./... and the auth test set pass. Both household homes were migrated off the pre-press token file and then proved live: auth status reports the right home rung, auth status --verify confirms the account with one call to Garmin, and the generated `account personal-information` command returns the matching userInfo.email through the generated HTTP client. The two homes report different account ids, and the legacy-config parse warning is gone from both.
